title: Far from the World, O Lord! I Flee
description: Far from the World, O Lord! I Flee in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 94, “Retirement”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Far from the world, O Lord! I flee, From strife and tu-mult far; From scenes where sin is wag-ing still Its most suc-cess-ful war.

lines: Far from the world, O Lord! I flee,
From strife and tumult far;
From scenes where sin is waging still
Its most successful war.
The calm retreat, the silent shade,
With prayer and praise agree;
And seem by Thy sweet bounty made,
For those who follow Thee.
There, if Thy presence cheer the soul,
And grace her mean abode,
O, with what peace, and joy, and love,
She communes with her God!
There, like the nightingale, she pours
Her solitary lays;
Nor asks a witness of her song,
Nor thirsts for human praise.
Author and Guardian of my life,
Sweet source of light divine,
And, — all harmonious names in one, —
My Father! Thou art mine!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
